I used **distinct call sites** (`file:line`), not distinct caller functions:

| Approach | Why |
|---|---|
| **Distinct call sites** (chosen) | Matches your request; a helper called in many tests/branches reflects real reuse pressure. |
| Distinct caller functions | Would undercount (e.g. `auth_test.go` alone contributes 19 sites across many test cases). |
| Raw textual matches | Would overcount declarations and non-call references. |

**Included:**
- Package-qualified calls via resolved import aliases, e.g. `util.GenUUID(...)`
- Explicit import aliases (`foo "…/internal/util"` — none found for `util`; all 12 importers use the default `util` name)

**Excluded:**
- The declaration itself (`func GenUUID()` at `util.go:40`)
- Comment/string matches (comments stripped before matching)

**Limitation:** Method calls are detected via `.Method(` when the callee’s package is imported. Calls through variables that **shadow** the package name (e.g. `profile.AllowAnonymous()` where `profile` is a `*profile.Profile` variable) can be missed. Even fixing that, the closest method candidate is `(Profile).AllowAnonymous` at **4** sites — still well below 28. Interface dispatch (e.g. `markdownService.ExtractAll`) is counted only when the selector matches a declared method name and the package is imported; those counts are small (≤2 per method).

Repo-wide sanity check (all Go, including `internal/` callers): `GenUUID` still leads at **28**; next is `scheduler.New` at **10**.
